A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeCo study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and inspecting revised qualitative examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing experiments, hallucination evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative analyses in Sections 2–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds MMVet results, coherence evaluations and a quantitative soft-modulation ablation.

M1.justification: The candidate-token selection, anchor-layer selection and dynamically weighted logit correction remain unchanged in Equations 3–7. Removing max_prob is an experimental ablation, while repetition penalties are suggested as a possible complement rather than introduced into DeCo.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds MMVet evaluation for LLaVA-1.5-7B and Qwen-VL-7B, covering recognition, OCR, knowledge, generation, spatial and mathematical categories. This modestly expands multimodal evaluation coverage; MSCOCO, POPE, MME and AMBER remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding CHAIR, POPE and AMBER comparisons retain Vanilla, DoLa, OPERA and VCD under their respective decoding strategies. MMVet uses the already established Vanilla comparator. The new component-removal control is a soft-modulation ablation.

E3.justification: The GPT-4o assessment adds a 1–10 coherence metric alongside accuracy and detailedness. New experiments evaluate MMVet using default nucleus-sampling settings and remove max_prob under greedy decoding while retaining the Table 2 images and prompts. Existing evaluation settings are otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a quantitative soft-modulation ablation beyond v1's illustrative example: removing max_prob raises CHAIR_S from 37.8 to 41.2 for LLaVA and 42.2 to 45.8 for Qwen. Figure 13 adds three supporting cases, and Figures 9–10 revise individual examples. Existing layer-perturbation and hyperparameter analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The added evaluations continue reporting point estimates without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and Table 4 accuracy/detailedness values remain unchanged. New MMVet results report Vanilla/DeCo totals of 23.6/27.9 for LLaVA and 45.7/46.3 for Qwen, with some Qwen subtask declines. v2 also adds coherence and soft-modulation results and revises qualitative outputs in Figures 9–10; these are supplemental findings, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the mathematical definitions remain unchanged. The added candidate-quality explanation and architectural speculation introduce no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same claims about preceding-layer visual information, suppression by language priors, training-free DeCo and its effectiveness and efficiency. The stated 10.8% average hallucination suppression and approximately 1.2-fold latency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds a speculative shared Transformer-attention explanation for LLM and MLLM hallucinations, including information loss and knowledge overshadowing. Section 4.4 adds guidance on balancing coherence through alpha, possible repetition penalties and model-specific layer selection. The original model-coverage and detailedness limitations are retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: Table 11 supplies the exact coherence-evaluation prompt. Appendices E–F document the new ablation control, its inherited images/prompts and MMVet decoding choice. Existing code-access information, A800 hardware, inference-time disclosure and core hyperparameter settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The expanded Appendix B connects the findings to LLM hallucination detection, attention anchors and knowledge overshadowing. References add INSIDE, Label Words Are Anchors, a knowledge-mechanisms survey and the knowledge-overshadowing work; VOLCANO's discussion and reference are removed. The original OPERA/VCD/DoLa positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes local explanatory edits, moves limitations and the method-comparison paragraph into appendices, and expands the appendix organization. It also updates affiliations and publication headers and adds acknowledgments. Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains coherence columns; new Tables 8–9 and 11 present the ablation, MMVet results and coherence prompt. Figure 13 is added, Figures 9–10 are revised, and several displays move or resize. The original evaluation prompt becomes Table 10, while the main graphical style and most displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 supported soft modulation mainly through an illustrative example; v2 adds a controlled quantitative ablation and further cases. Coherence scores make output-quality tradeoffs more assessable, and MMVet modestly broadens validation. These strengthen the paper incrementally: the central method and results remain stable, uncertainty reporting is unchanged, and the new architectural explanation remains speculative.
